source_units.text:
Animal to Human Translation of Voriconazole
Feasibility study   Version 1.0 (draft)   9 October 2026
Objective and available data
We will test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human voriconazole exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation. Voriconazole is a known-drug test case with existing human PK for independent validation. The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability. Following the translational objective of Sou et al. (2021), we do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.
Drug and data files. Voriconazole is the sole test drug; fluconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, amphotericin B, caspofungin and tofacitinib appear in the sources as comparators or co-administered drugs and are not substitutes. Voriconazole_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes, not a ready-made modeling dataset:
Mouse: digitized mean plasma curves and exposure parameters after oral doses in non-neutropenic aspergillosis mice, serum PK parameters and per-isolate efficacy in neutropenic candidiasis mice, intraperitoneal PK and survival ED50s against A. flavus, and serum levels in mice given grapefruit juice. Two studies sampled PK on day 2 of treatment, and exposure rises more than dose-proportionally. Use for PK and eligible PD analysis; kidney CFU and survival endpoints are not interchangeable.
Rat: single IV and oral PK with and without a co-administered drug, a population model with saturable elimination and autoinduction from 10-day intraperitoneal dosing with model-predicted AUCs, and a population model with plasma binding in healthy and meningitis rats. Use for systemic PK, nonlinearity and time-dependent clearance.
Cross_species_secondary: one multi-species table (mouse, rat, rabbit, guinea pig, dog) reproduced in a thesis from Roffey et al. (2003), with single- and multiple-dose AUC after IV and oral dosing and protein binding. The original paper was not available, the column-to-species mapping is unverified, and decimals use Portuguese commas. Use it only as low-confidence context or for sensitivity analysis, never as the sole basis for a species model.
In_vitro_MIC: EUCAST MIC distributions for C. albicans and A. fumigatus, and isolate MICs for the two mouse aspergillosis studies (candidiasis isolate MICs sit with their efficacy table on the Mouse sheet). Use matched isolate MICs for PD and the distributions for population-weighted attainment; a distribution cannot replace matched isolate MICs.
Human validation data are not in this package. Human reference tables (label PK parameters and statements, a healthy-volunteer IV-to-oral dose-escalation study, and a human-target column removed from a rat source) are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
Other files. Voriconazole_project_proposal.docx defines this task. AGENT_README.md explains package use and known gaps.
Tasks to complete
1. Prepare the data. Split the mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs. Check provenance, units, dose histories, treatment day, analytes, matrices, assays, experimental units and missing fields. Identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.
2. Fit animal PK. Select eligible systemic PK models for mouse and rat, including saturable elimination and time-dependent clearance where the data support them. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits. Document whether and how the secondary multi-species table is used.

3. Predict human PK. Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, metabolic clearance and justified physiological relationships, accounting for nonlinearity and autoinduction before scaling. Compare approaches with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.
4. Determine the PK/PD index. For eligible data, compare fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, separately by organism and endpoint. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target.
5. Validate the human prediction. Apply the frozen model to the doses and regimens in the human reference tables. Compare predicted and observed plasma PK, including the change from single to repeated dosing. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.
6. Produce PTA and assess feasibility. After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and IV and oral dosing scenarios to estimate the probability of target attainment (PTA) at each MIC. Process the MIC distributions and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver the PTA tables/curves, feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.
Essential rules
1. Preserve evidence level. Keep source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters, model-predicted AUCs and digitized points are not individual animals or observations. Keep the secondary multi-species table labelled as secondary throughout. Do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements.
2. Keep biological quantities compatible. Separate routes (oral gavage, intraperitoneal, IV), total versus unbound drug, serum versus plasma versus free brain dialysate, and bioassay versus chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats, so parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Every conversion requires a recorded justification. Binding sources conflict (mouse 78% bound in serum versus 29.97% unbound in plasma versus 67% in the secondary table; rat 64-66%); never average them, and carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.
3. Give all three indices equal eligibility and both regression families. Compare them on the same matched response records, isolate MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner. Keep CFU-based and survival-based targets separate; a target from one organism or endpoint cannot set another.
4. Prevent leakage. Published ED50s, exposure indices and conclusions cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings. The rat escalating regimen was designed to match a human exposure target; do not use it to tune scaling. Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling. Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

5. Process MIC and PTA explicitly. Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators, censored categories and test method (EUCAST, CLSI or NCCLS). The EUCAST distributions were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs, and the C. albicans data are mostly truncated at 0.016 mg/L; do not read them as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize. Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment. Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty; group summaries cannot supply invented interindividual variability.
6. Limit and document conclusions. A successful fit is not predictive validation; human PK agreement does not validate antifungal efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps. Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results, and obtain human review before fitting.
Reference: Sou T et al. Model-Informed Drug Development for Antimicrobials: Translational PK and PK/PD Modeling to Predict an Efficacious Human Dose for Apramycin. Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics. 2021;109:1063-1073. https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.2104

steps.adequacy: Assess current input requirements and data coverage; planning later outputs is not requiring them now.
steps.prepare: Prepare permitted data and preserve provenance, units, experimental identity and missingness.
steps.eda: Exploratory analysis, only if that separate workflow step is enabled.
steps.dispatch: Assign an approved task, data and applicable constraints to a downstream analysis.
steps.animal_pk: Fit, select and evaluate animal PK models.
steps.pk_translation: Scale animal models and predict held-out species and human PK before opening validation outcomes.
steps.index: Compare PK/PD indices and qualify effect targets.
steps.human_validation: After the required freezes, compare frozen human predictions with permitted human observations.
steps.pta: After the stated prerequisites, simulate per-MIC and MIC-weighted attainment and its uncertainty.
steps.clinical: Interpret and report feasibility, scientific limitations and final benchmarks; use specific validation or PTA steps for their distinct requirements.
